question.problem:
$$
r(y,\theta )=⟨{e}^{1-{y}^{2}}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y,\,\text{_______}⟩
$$

The vector-valued function $r(y,\theta )$ above parametrizes the surface of revolution generated by rotating the curve $x={e}^{1-{y}^{2}}$ by $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis for $y\in [\frac{1}{2},2].$ What is the third component of $r?$
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14275690/assets/be6fb27c0d050a7007e9f4a0d526daaff40b8f7d01f20c63ac8cc00074121f28.png)

 

A point $(x,y,z)$ on the surface generated by rotating the graph of $x=f(y)$ by $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis has the position vector

$$
\begin{aligned}r=⟨f(y)\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y,\,f(y)\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩,\,y\in [a,b],\,\theta =[0,2\pi ).\end{aligned}
$$

First, notice that $x=f(y)={e}^{1-{y}^{2}}\ge 0$ for all $y\in [\frac{1}{2},2].$ 

So, the parametrization of our surface of revolution is 

$$
r(y,\theta )=⟨{e}^{1-{y}^{2}}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y,\,{e}^{1-{y}^{2}}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩,\,y\in [\frac{1}{2},2],\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

  

Therefore, the third component of $r$ is ${e}^{1-{y}^{2}}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .$
